messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: per-model TPS anomaly detected for model-family: zephyr-7b. 5m sustained spike; error-rate increase on tail calls. auto-mitigation suggested: apply temporary RPM/TPM cap. link: https://incidents.internal/2039001234 :rotating_light:

nina: saw the alert, paging SRE oncall. i'll take first look. @matt can you grab traces?

matt: on it. pulling traces now, looks like a burst from a handful of clients hitting long-context streaming paths. some infinite-loop user-provided prompts causing large token streams.

olivia: adding context — zephyr-7b has lower perf at >8k windows; manifests as queued requests + higher p99 latency.

eli: tagging infra-bot to check per-pool saturation and autoscaler activity. @infra-bot status?

infra-bot: pool zephyr-prod-1: gpu_util 96%, queue_len 122, avg_lat_p99 2.7s, current_tpm_config: {"rpm":1200,"tpm":24000}. autoscaler: no new nodes started in last 3m (scaling disabled due to maintenance flag).

nina: okay, critical path is high TPM, and autoscale disabled — that explains persistent queue. mitigation options: (1) temporary TPM/RPM reduction on zephyr family, (2) enable burst autoscale, (3) route low-priority customers to zephyr-quant variant. prefer (1)+(3) for fastest effect.

matt: we should also consider aborting very long streaming sessions. can we apply a per-request token cap?

eli: token cap rollout is riskier; quick wins: reduce per-model RPM to 600 and TMP to 12k, and bump zephyr-quant routing to accept low-cost tier. I can push via admin API.

nina: please include a canary: change for 5m then assess. post pre/post metrics. also notify support + customers with >500 rps.

eli: running command now:

```
# admin API
POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/quotas/update
{
  "model_family": "zephyr-7b",
  "overrides": {"rpm": "600", "tpm": "12000"},
  "scope": "runtime",
  "reason": "live surge containment - 2039001234",
  "duration": "5m",
  "dry_run": false
}
```

infra-bot: quota update accepted, rollout_id=rl-7b-2039, applying to zephyr-prod-1..3. expected propagation: ~30s.

matt: seeing immediate drop in incoming accepted requests on zephyr-prod-1, queue_len -> 34. error-rate for tail calls down 45% in 40s.

olivia: routing change: promoting zephyr-quant for low-priority label users. command: `route:update zephyr-quant +label:low-priority capacity:20pct`

eli: done. infra-bot reports zephyr-quant incoming load +18%. p99 latency on zephyr-prod normalized to 1.1s.

nina: good. can we capture affected customer ids for follow-up? need to coordinate comms and possible crediting.

matt: extracted top 8 client ids driving burst; pushing to #support-alerts with notes.

olivia: checking logs for token-abuse patterns. two clients had automated loops hitting streaming continue calls. I asked security to reach out.

nina: action items: 1) keep quota caps for 10m unless metrics stable; 2) support to notify impacted customers; 3) eng-runtime to re-enable autoscale maintenance flag after validation; 4) security to contact abusive clients.

eli: extending override to 10m now (updating duration). API call returns success.

infra-bot: override rl-7b-2039 extended to 10m. scheduled rollback at 2039002500 unless modified.

matt: monitoring for regressions. p50/p90 stable, p99 trending down.

nina: thanks team. i'll stay in thread for handoff. @matt once p99 < 1.4s for 5m, handoff to daytime oncall.

matt: will do. current p99=1.08s, sustained 90s.

olivia: note for postmortem: consider deploy safety that prevents autoscale dead flags during peak. also add an eval to detect loop-y prompt patterns for streaming endpoints.

nina: agreed. documenting this in incident tracker. final status: mitigation applied (per-model rpm/tpm reduction + routing to quant variant), customer impact limited (rate-limited but service continued), follow-ups assigned.

infra-bot: THREAD CLOSED: mitigation active, scheduled rollback at 2039002500. escalate if metrics worsen. :white_check_mark:
